the formation of surface relief gratings under the action of high-power radiation on an absorbing medium is due to a combination of two processes: the thermal effect of the radiation on the absorbing medium and its diffraction on the surface relief of the medium.

a periodic structure is formed on the surface of an absorbing dielectric or semiconductor when the following conditions are met: (1) the surface roughness is of the order of the wavelength of the incident wave; (2) the optical constants of the medium are such that the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index differ by a factor of the order of unity; and (3) the optical constants vary periodically along the surface of the medium.
, in general, the formation of a surface grating is possible only if the surface is inhomogeneous and the medium has a high absorption coefficient.
